title: autopilot.yaml
description: Per-project configuration for the Autopilot runner. One file per Linear project, kept in ~/.config/autopilot/projects/<name>.yaml (or the project's main repo). It holds no secrets.

name.description: Short slug; used for state files and report headings.

projects.description: Linear project names this config covers. Issues delegated to Autopilot in other projects are not worked.

states.description: Workflow state names; each may also be a state type (started, completed, ...).

waiting.description: Waiting for something that clears by itself (a check, another ticket). Never a started state.

blocked.description: Waiting for the owner's answer (wait: owner): the issue shows as Blocked and the owner is @mentioned in a top-level comment. An unstarted-type state; falls back to waiting if the team lacks it.

followup_state.description: Where follow-up tickets the worker files go. Never a state that Autopilot works from.

release_checks_project.description: Linear project for owner-only checks left after an issue is Done on preprod (device QA, second-user, admin), gone through before a prod release. Without it the worker blocks on such checks.

owner.description: Linear name or email of the human who gets notices outside an issue (e.g. the preprod keep-alive's sign-in notice is assigned to them).

repos.description: Repositories tickets may change. Empty = Linear-only tasks (answers, triage, docs in Linear), unless new_repos lets an issue start one.

path.description: The shared checkout. Read-only for Autopilot: workers use git worktrees.

house_rules.description: A file the worker reads before coding.

setup.description: Commands that prepare a fresh worktree ($WT is the worktree).

checks.description: Local checks that must pass before a PR.

deploy_workflows.description: Workflows that deploy preprod after a merge to the default branch.

ci_review.description: The repo's CI runs the AI review: a check reviews every push and an account approves the head commit when it passes (or requests changes). With it, the worker runs no code-review or general reviewer rounds of its own on this repo. It fixes what the CI review flags and merges on that check plus that approval of the head, with no open review threads. The security reviewer still runs where the review table or a config note requires it.

check.description: The CI check that runs the review, e.g. claude-review.

approver.description: The login whose APPROVED review of the head commit is the AI approval, e.g. github-actions[bot].

checks_attack_closed.description: The CI review also checks a PR's 'Attack closed' section (copied from the issue) and blocks when the attack isn't closed. Then the worker runs no security reviewer of its own on this repo.

new_repos.description: Optional: an issue with a 'New repo: <name>' line written by linear.owner (needed with this) may start a new repository (worker section 2a). The run creates it with the owner's gh login (the GitHub App has no Administration permission), clones it, adds it to this config's repos and lands the issue's scaffold through a PR. Without it, such an issue blocks and asks. Off unless set.

owner.description: The GitHub organization or user new repos are created under. A 'New repo:' line naming another owner blocks.

path_root.description: Folder the shared checkout is cloned into, as <path_root>/<name>.

template.description: A template repository to create new repos from. Without it a repo starts with only a README.

repo_defaults.description: Copied into the new repo's repos entry. The scaffold PR fills in checks when this leaves them out.

ticket_id_in_branch_or_title.description: Keep false: Linear auto-completes a ticket whose ID is in a merged PR's branch or title, before preprod verification.

policy.description: merge-all: merge every green, AI-reviewed PR. hold-sensitive: leave PRs touching hold_paths for the owner. never: open PRs only.

hold_paths.description: Globs that count as security/schema changes under hold-sensitive.

admin_on_missing_approval.description: Only without the Autopilot GitHub App (github: owner): allow `gh pr merge --admin` when the merge is refused for a missing approval (owner-authored PRs can't be self-approved). Never past a failing check. With the app, a missing approval blocks and asks the owner to approve.

code_review.description: Effort for the Claude Code code-review skill run on every PR before the reviewer subagents. off: a correctness subagent instead. ultra is not allowed (billed, owner-triggered).

preprod.description: Where and how merged work is verified. Omit for projects with no preprod.

api_hosts.description: Hosts the preprod app must call; anything else means wrong environment.

every_hours.description: The scheduled fast exit wakes a run after 20 h, so more than that is never honoured.

user.description: The test user who must be signed in there (a test_users name).

session_jwt_storage_key.description: localStorage key of the session JWT. The keep-alive decodes only its exp claim, never prints or sends it.

warn_hours.description: File a sign-in notice when the session has less than this left. Not with sign_in: the first visit after the session ends signs in again.

sign_in.description: Optional: sign a test user back in on the login screen with a local password filler, without Autopilot ever seeing the password (orchestrator section 1c). Without it Autopilot never signs in: it asks the owner.

with.description: passhand: the Passhand MCP server's fill_login fills the login saved for the tab's origin, in Chrome (preprod.browser: chrome).

user.description: The test user signed in this way (a test_users name), and the one that must show as signed in afterwards. Default: keepalive.user; set it only without a keepalive, or to the same name.

username.description: The username saved in Passhand, if it isn't the test user's name (e.g. an email address).

keep_signed_in.description: Label of a 'keep me signed in' checkbox to tick before signing in, e.g. 'Keep me logged in'.

browser_host.description: Optional: a long-lived Chromium of Autopilot's own on this Mac (bin/autopilot-browser), for browser drivers that connect over CDP, e.g. Playwright MCP with --cdp-endpoint. Only web_url's host, api_hosts and allow_hosts resolve there. The keep-alive (orchestrator section 1b) starts it and keeps its test user signed in, with Passhand when sign_in is set. Off unless set.

user.description: The test user signed in there (a test_users name), and the name that must show on keepalive.url. Default: sign_in.user, else keepalive.user. Prefer a test user of its own: one user's sessions in two browsers can end each other (a sign-out in either ends them all).

username.description: The username saved in Passhand for that user, if it isn't the name. Default: sign_in.username when user is sign_in's user.

allow_hosts.description: Hosts the app needs besides web_url's and api_hosts (a font or asset CDN). Every other host fails to resolve. Never a forbidden.hosts host.

dismiss.description: Button text of first-run prompts to click away, e.g. 'Maybe Later' on an install banner that blocks clicks in a fresh profile.

sign_in_button.description: Visible text of the login form's sign-in button (matched whole, in any case).

known_fixes.description: Mechanical owner steps the worker quotes exactly in an elicitation's 'What I need from you'.

forbidden.description: Hard no-prod rules. Phase 4 hooks enforce these; until then the skills state them.

coder.description: The implementation step on a non-Claude model through OpenRouter (bin/autopilot-coder), only for an issue with a coder:<model> label or a 'Coder model:' line. Its cost counts against spend.paid_model_usd_per_ticket.

enabled.description: false: an issue that names a non-Claude model blocks and asks, instead of coding on it.

models.description: Short names an issue may use, to OpenRouter model ids, e.g. deepseek: deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash. Other names are matched against OpenRouter's model list.

paid_model_usd_per_ticket.description: Gemini/Vertex or other paid model spend a ticket may cause in total.
